hints: Focus on the word organic product, so first work out what carbon-containing product each reagent makes with ethanoic acid.
Recall the four familiar reactions: reduction gives ethanol, metal and carbonate give ethanoate salts, alcohol gives an ester.
Now compare Mr values by adding the atoms together, and notice what happens when two ethanoate groups join to one metal ion.
walkthrough:
**Identify the type of reaction for each reagent**

Think of ethanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$, as both an acid and a carboxylic acid. It can be reduced, neutralised, or esterified.

$$\text{acid + metal, carbonate, alcohol, or LiAlH}_4 \rightarrow \text{different organic product}$$

**Write the organic product in each case**

Lovely, let's list them side by side so we can compare.

$$\text{A: CH}_3\text{COOH} \xrightarrow{\text{LiAlH}_4} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH (ethanol)}$$ 
$$\text{B: 2CH}_3\text{COOH} + \text{Mg} \rightarrow \text{(CH}_3\text{COO)}_2\text{Mg} + \text{H}_2$$
$$\text{C: 2CH}_3\text{COOH} + \text{K}_2\text{CO}_3 \rightarrow \text{2CH}_3\text{COOK} + \text{CO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
$$\text{D: CH}_3\text{COOH} + \text{(CH}_3)_2\text{CHOH} \rightleftharpoons \text{CH}_3\text{COOCH(CH}_3)_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Calculate Mr of each organic product**

Now just add up the relative masses. Remember $\text{CH}_3\text{COO}$ is 59.

$$M_r(\text{ethanol, C}_2\text{H}_6\text{O}) = 46$$
$$M_r(\text{(CH}_3\text{COO)}_2\text{Mg}) = (59 \times 2) + 24 = 142$$
$$M_r(\text{CH}_3\text{COOK}) = 59 + 39 = 98$$
$$M_r(\text{CH}_3\text{COOCH(CH}_3)_2, \text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}\text{O}_2) = 102$$
The magnesium salt contains two ethanoate ions per formula unit, so it is clearly the heaviest.

options.A: LiAlH4 is a strong reducing agent and reduces ethanoic acid to the primary alcohol, ethanol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$. With Mr = 46 this is the lightest organic product, not the heaviest.
options.B: Magnesium neutralises the acid: $\text{2CH}_3\text{COOH + Mg} \rightarrow \text{(CH}_3\text{COO)}_2\text{Mg + H}_2$. The organic product magnesium ethanoate contains two ethanoate groups, giving Mr about 142, the highest of the four.
options.C: Potassium carbonate neutralises the acid: $\text{2CH}_3\text{COOH + K}_2\text{CO}_3 \rightarrow \text{2CH}_3\text{COOK + CO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$. The organic product potassium ethanoate has Mr = 98, which is less than the magnesium salt because it has only one ethanoate per formula unit.
options.D: Propan-2-ol esterifies the acid to give the ester isopropyl ethanoate, $\text{CH}_3\text{COOCH(CH}_3)_2$. With formula $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}\text{O}_2$, Mr = 102. This is a common trap as esters feel large, but it is still lighter than the magnesium salt.
